objective: An approval means something was checked (Ruling D46). An empty assessment cannot pass. Every verdict that can block has a consumer. A check that compared nothing says so. Every judge that keeps a loop going tells the next attempt why.
evidence: autornd/models/verdicts.py:347-354: when green is unset, _resolve_green derives green = not has_cause. ValidateVerdict defaults green and red_cause to None and evidence to [], so an empty JSON object validates green. ImplementVerdict's summary may be empty, and judges read implement.green, which is resolved the same way (review B finding 1; verified by the advisor against main 4fda54f).

workflows/engineering-rnd.yaml:322 and workflows/independent-check-probe.yaml:63: independent_check returns a DoubleCheckVerdict whose ship field no gate reads. The run can complete after the one reviewer that sees unrecallable work says not to ship.

autornd/engine/phases.py:397: feasibility appends its hard blockers to plan.blockers after plan_ready has already passed. They can never stop a run, and they are misrecorded as plan blockers (open since 098). phases.py:768 then hands them to implement as 'FEASIBILITY CONCERNS (from domain specialist review — address these)'. That opens a second criteria channel after D43 closed the plan's scope (review A F5).

autornd/graph/checks.py:755-790: numbers_consistent reports 'no contradicting values' when the plan and the implementation share no unit, so 'compared nothing' reads as 'consistent'. It also passes a unit when any one plan value agrees with any one implementation value (review B finding 10). That second point is recorded here, not changed: the checks' fate waits for the tier-2 data.

autornd/graph/adapter.py:583 writes a failure-log entry only when validate or implement is red. The judges fold also refuses convergence on a coverage miss or a consistency conflict, so the loop can go round again without telling the implementer why (review B finding 9).

autornd/engine/phases.py (feasibility's channel, and the implement prompt's heading for it)
workflows/engineering-rnd.yaml and workflows/independent-check-probe.yaml (independent_check's terminal gate only)

constraints: RULING FIRST, VERBATIM, in HANDOVER.md and the notebook, before the code in commit order.

RULING D46, COMMITTED VERBATIM: 'Ruling D46 (advisor, 2026-10-02) — an approval means something was checked. (1) A validation verdict with no evidence cannot be green, and an implementation with no deliverable cannot be green; either resolves red, with a cause that names what was missing, and is counted. The resolution of green from red_cause otherwise stands. (2) Every verdict that can block has a consumer. The independent check's do-not-ship ends the run blocked, with its findings. The feasibility review runs after the plan gate and cannot stop a run, so it no longer writes plan blockers; its concerns reach the implementer as considerations a reviewer raised, not as requirements. (3) A check that compared nothing says so: it passes as before, but it is recorded as not checked, and the terminal record lists every check that did not check. (4) Every judge that keeps a loop going writes its reason into the failure log, so the next attempt is told why. D36's plan rules and D43's scope rule are untouched. Rationale: the 2026-10-02 outside review (docs/reviews/2026-10-02-consultant-reviews.md), verified by the advisor: an empty validation object passed (verdicts.py:351); the independent check's verdict had no consumer; feasibility blockers were recorded as plan blockers and handed to the implementer as 'address these' after D43 closed the plan's scope; numbers_consistent reported 'no contradicting values' when it had compared none; and a consistency-only failure looped with no failure-log entry (adapter.py:583). Falsifier: a green verdict with no evidence or no deliverable, a blocking verdict with no consumer, or a loop iteration whose cause is missing from the failure log.'

GREEN NEEDS SUBSTANCE: in _resolve_green, a ValidateVerdict with no evidence cannot be green, and neither can an ImplementVerdict whose summary is empty or whitespace. Either resolves red, with a red_cause that names what was missing ('the validator returned no assessment'; 'the implementation returned no deliverable'), and is counted under a new normalisation kind. The rest of the ruled truth table stands.

A CONSUMER FOR EVERY BLOCKING VERDICT: add a terminal gate after independent_check in both workflow files. A do-not-ship ends the run blocked, with the verdict's findings in the reason; the gate must not route into a loop. Feasibility no longer writes plan.blockers. Its concerns travel in feasibility's own output, and the implement prompt renders them under a heading that calls them considerations a reviewer raised, not requirements. Quote the new heading and the old one. The gate carries independent_check's own `when: triage.unrecallable`, because a gate that reads a path the skipped node never wrote raises (hard rule 3; graph/conditions.py).

NOT CHECKED IS NOT CONSISTENT: the check Result gains a checked flag, default true. numbers_consistent sets it false when the plan and the implementation share no unit; criteria_addressed sets it false when there are no criteria. Pass and fail do not change, and the fold treats an unchecked check as non-blocking. The run's terminal record lists every check that did not check.

THE NEXT ATTEMPT IS TOLD WHY: whenever the judges fold refuses convergence, the adapter writes a failure-log entry naming every judge that refused, with its conflicts or misses, whether or not validate and implement are red. No entry is written twice for one iteration.

TESTS, through the real builders, the real executor and the provider-free test doubles: (a) {} as a validate verdict resolves red and is counted, and so does an empty implement summary. (b) independent_check with ship false ends the run blocked, with its findings. (c) Feasibility concerns are absent from plan.blockers; the implement prompt carries them under the considerations heading; D36 and D43 are byte-identical. (d) numbers_consistent with no shared unit passes with checked false, and the terminal record lists it. (e) A consistency-only failure writes a failure-log entry naming consistency, and the next implement prompt carries it. Prove each by breaking. Rule 7: for every existing test this changes, say which of the two was wrong.
